title: Ra and the Sun
objective: After this level you can explain the sun god Ra's daily journey.
summary: Egyptians believed Ra sailed across the sky by day and through the underworld by night, beating the serpent Apophis to be reborn every dawn.

cards.headline: Every sunset, Egyptians believed, the Sun set off on a dangerous night voyage.
cards.body: And every sunrise meant it had made it back. Meet Ra, the sun god, and the trip he made every single day.

cards.headline: The Sun takes the boat
cards.body: Ra was the god of the Sun and a creator god, worshipped above all at Heliopolis. He was often shown as a man with a falcon’s head and a sun disk on top. Egyptians believed he crossed the sky each day in a boat, his solar bark. That fits a land whose great highway was the Nile, where boats were the easiest way to travel (remember Level 5?). If you lived by the river, why would the Sun walk?

cards.headline: The night shift
cards.body: At sunset, Ra didn’t clock off. Egyptians believed he boarded another boat and sailed through the underworld all night. Waiting there was his great enemy, Apophis, an evil serpent. Ra had to defeat the serpent every night to be born again for the new day. So a sunrise wasn’t just morning. It was a victory, won in the dark, every single day.
cards.callout: Day: sail the sky. Night: beat the serpent. Dawn: born again.

mascot.line: Next time you watch a sunrise, remember: to an Egyptian, the Sun had just survived the night.

cards.fact: Egyptians believed the Sun was born again every morning.
cards.context: Ra’s night voyage through the underworld ended in rebirth for the new day. Death-like darkness, then new life: hold on to that pattern. It runs through the rest of this chapter.

cards.headline: Ra’s journey: traced
learned: Ra, the sun god, crossed the sky in a boat
At night he sailed through the underworld
He defeated the serpent Apophis every night
Egyptians believed the Sun was reborn each dawn

questions.prompt: What did Egyptians believe Ra used to cross the sky each day?

options.label: A chariot
options.rationale: Ra traveled by water, even in the sky.

options.label: A falcon’s wings
options.rationale: He had a falcon’s head, but he traveled by boat.

options.label: A ladder of stars
options.rationale: No ladder: the solar bark carried him.

questions.explanation: Egyptians pictured Ra sailing across the sky in a boat, his solar bark.

questions.prompt: In Egyptian belief, why was every sunrise a kind of victory?

options.label: Ra had defeated the serpent Apophis during the night
Priests had pushed the Sun up with ropes
options.rationale: The struggle was Ra’s own, in the underworld.

options.label: The Nile had flooded overnight
options.rationale: The flood came once a year, not every night.

options.label: Seth had given the Sun back

questions.explanation: Egyptians believed Ra fought Apophis every night in the underworld and was born again at dawn.

questions.prompt: Why does it make sense that Egyptians pictured their sun god traveling by boat?

options.label: Egypt had no roads at all
options.rationale: The point is that the river was the easiest route.

options.label: The Sun was thought to be made of water
options.rationale: Ra was a god of the Sun, not of water.

options.label: Boats on the Nile were Egypt’s easiest way to travel
Ra was said to have built the first boat
options.rationale: Nothing in the myth says so.

questions.explanation: The Nile was Egypt’s great highway, so a sun god on a boat matched how Egyptians themselves got around.
